Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G2556; not bad, i.e. (objectively) innocent or (subjectively) unsuspecting:--harmless, simple.
BiblicalUsage: Twice, in opposite directions. Paul warns that smooth talkers deceive the hearts of the simple — the innocent, the unsuspecting; and Hebrews says our High Priest is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for harmless carries little weight on its own; its weight is the contrast between the simple sheep and the harmless Shepherd, one innocent by ignorance and one by holiness.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
